accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1 and 3 / ass:reached-eigen-band and ass:reached-projector-band
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The finite-sample guarantee is conditional on public lower gaps only at matrix and projector comparisons reached by the fixed population transcript; it does not establish their necessity for all CRL learners.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Recover-or-abstain graph and encoder guarantees, and the strict spectral relaxation, hold under the declared transcript-local eigen and projector bands plus the stated Gaussian perfect-intervention model.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Equation (22) is the minimum positive eigenvalue over all subset sums, equation (23) is the product \(\min_i\|G^\dagger_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\), and Theorem 1 uses separate \(\eta\) and \(\gamma\) thresholds for graph recovery; Lemma 19 targets the transitive closure.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 14-20, score-difference range identities and Section 5 linear-transformation recovery
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops score-difference CRL geometry and a linear-transformation recovery procedure using one hard intervention per node.
The paper develops time-uniform confidence sequences, matrix-martingale bounds, and a covariance-estimation application.
The paper studies injectively linearly mixed linear latent causal models and states that one perfect intervention per latent variable is sufficient for identifiability.
Corollary 4.5 gives a deterministic Boolean-complexity algorithm producing an operator-norm-accurate spectral projector for a Hermitian-definite pencil.
